A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MINGLE research work. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original continual-merging experiments, MTIL comparisons, corruption tests, and ablations in Section 4 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains original vision experiments and adds language-task results, adaptation-budget experiments, inference measurements, and forward-transfer results.

M1.justification: The low-rank expert construction, KL adaptation objective, freezing of earlier gates, and adaptive null-space gating remain intact. Revised covariance descriptions and projection notation do not establish a different algorithm; evaluation on Flan-T5 alone is not a method change.

E1.justification: v2 adds eight GLUE language tasks with Flan-T5-base, extending evaluation from image classification to text processing (Table 2). The original vision task groups, MTIL benchmark, and seven image corruptions remain.

E2.justification: The main vision comparison adds Consensus TA, continual layer-wise AdaMerging, and continual LoRA-WEMOE (Tables 1 and 13). AdaMerging previously participated only in the corruption comparison. LoRA-WEMOE also joins that comparison alongside the retained original WEMOE, rather than merely renaming it.

E3.justification: New protocols include alphabetical GLUE evaluation with Flan-T5-base and 100 unlabeled adaptation samples, a 5/10/20/50-step adaptation sweep, and throughput and forward-transfer measurements. Existing vision defaults and task-order lists remain unchanged. The revised seed-sample analysis no longer reports the 20-samples-per-class condition.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's component, rank, layer, gate, and sample-count analyses, v2 adds adaptation-step sensitivity (Table 6), adaptation-time scaling (Table 7b), comparative inference/storage analysis (Table 15), and forward transfer (Table 16). Most earlier analyses are retained; the seed-sample analysis is reformatted and its 20-sample point omitted.

E5.justification: Both versions report vision results as mean and standard deviation across ten task orders using seeds 42–51, and gate-activation variability across layers. Additional result rows do not introduce a new uncertainty procedure, increased run count, confidence interval, or significance test.

E6.justification: v2 adds GLUE results, including MINGLE's reported 83.3 ACC and 0.1 BWT, full-configuration ViT-L/14 results, and budget, inference, and forward-transfer findings. Existing appendix values also change: MINGLE's 20-task ViT-B/16 EuroSAT accuracy changes from 84.7 to 90.0 (v1 Table 9; v2 Table 13). The earlier ViT-L/14 MINGLE row is retained under MINGLE*, avoiding a false same-configuration comparison.

T1.justification: The dynamic-MoE risk theorem, assumptions, and three-part Appendix A proof retain their substance; the appendix theorem is renumbered and boxed. The added forward-transfer formula supports an empirical metric rather than introducing a new theoretical result.

C1.justification: Both versions claim TTCMM, MINGLE with adaptive null-space gating, improved robustness and forgetting resistance, and a 7–9% average advantage. Calling TTCMM a task and MINGLE its framework clarifies an existing distinction rather than redefining the core contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations of sub-unit gate activations through expert complementarity, interpretations of inference efficiency and forward transfer, and deployment and privacy arguments in Appendix D. It also explicitly contrasts TTCMM with rehearsal-free continual learning. The original shared-initialization and identical-backbone limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds baseline hyperparameters and resource requirements (Tables 11–12), NLP sampling details, expanded timing information, and a MINGLE code-access link. These substantially expand reproducibility documentation. Conversely, v1's explicit RTX 4090 identification and CLIP logit construction are removed; the new checklist retains a submission-time code-release promise.

R1.justification: Four cited works are added: instruction-finetuned language models, GLUE, Twin-merging, and task localization underlying Consensus TA. Related-work discussion expands dynamic-merging positioning and the relationship to rehearsal-free learning, while retaining the original literature framework. Publication-metadata updates concern existing citations.

P1.justification: The abstract, related-work survey, experimental narrative, and conclusion receive substantial rewriting. v2 also reorganizes analysis and discussion subsections and adds acknowledgments and a NeurIPS checklist, while preserving the overall introduction–method–experiments structure.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands comparison-table structures, adds assumption columns and several new tables, and combines the earlier efficiency table and seed-sample plot into multipart Table 7. Existing plots are largely retained and renumbered; the appendix contents and theorem gain boxed layouts.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's vision-only evaluation and mainly static main-table comparators, v2 adds language evaluation and directly tests relevant adaptive and dynamic competitors. Budget and inference analyses, explicit comparator assumptions, and baseline settings substantially strengthen assessment of the claimed advantages and practical costs. These gains outweigh localized reporting weaknesses, including omitted GPU identification and inconsistent MINGLE* parameter counts between Tables 7 and 15.
